prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrat Manifesto 2010 — Summary (under 500 words)

Core aim: Hard‑wire fairness into national life by redistributing power – economic, social, political and financial – through four priorities:
- Fair taxes that put money back in your pocket
- A fair chance for every child
- A fair future, creating green jobs and a sustainable economy
- A fair deal by cleaning up politics and restoring civil liberties

Fair taxes and public finances
- Raise the income tax threshold to £10,000 (c. £700 tax cut for most; 3.6m taken out of income tax), funded by: restricting pension tax relief to basic rate; taxing capital gains at income rates; anti-avoidance measures; per‑plane duty replacing Air Passenger Duty (higher for non‑lifeline domestic flights); 1% Mansion Tax on property value above £2m; reform of non‑dom status.
- Credible deficit plan: over £15bn identified savings; timing of cuts from 2011–12 subject to economic tests. Measures include: £400 cap on public sector pay rises for two years; bank levy; scrap ID cards/biometric passports/ContactPoint; cancel Eurofighter Tranche 3B; reform prisons (presumption against short sentences); scale back quangos/inspection regimes; IT procurement reform. Oppose like‑for‑like Trident replacement; full defence review.

Economy, jobs and green transition
- Break up banks (separate retail/investment), get lending going, curb bonus culture; create Local Enterprise Funds and Regional Stock Exchanges.
- One‑year green stimulus creating c.100,000 jobs: shipyard refurbishment for offshore renewables; Eco Cash‑Back for home efficiency/micro‑generation; school/public building insulation; bus scrappage; bring 250,000 empty homes into use; major youth opportunity programme.
- Establish a UK Infrastructure Bank to crowd in private capital for energy/transport (including high‑speed rail); promote superfast broadband; cut red tape; reform business rates to site value; fairer takeover rules; support mutuals, co‑ops and Royal Mail/Post Office reform.

Education and skills
- £2.5bn Pupil Premium targeted at disadvantaged pupils to cut class sizes, expand one‑to‑one support, SEN assessments, teacher training, anti‑bullying.
- Slimmed curriculum and independent standards authority; fair admissions and local accountability; “Sponsor‑Managed Schools” model; inclusive faith school policies.
- Phase out university tuition fees over six years (final‑year fees scrapped immediately); national bursary scheme; more foundation degrees and adult apprenticeships; end Train to Gain for large firms.

NHS and care
- Protect frontline services by cutting bureaucracy; integrate health and social care; elected Local Health Boards; patient entitlements to timely diagnosis/treatment; GP choice and email access; boost dementia research, mental health therapies; targeted alcohol and air‑quality measures.
- Independent commission on long‑term care; immediate carers’ respite.

Families, work and consumers
- Shared parental leave and flexible working for all; strengthen child protection; youth services statutory; restore earnings link for state pension (triple‑lock style); scrap compulsory retirement age; long‑term goal of Citizen’s Pension.
- Fairer energy tariffs (cheaper lifeline block), social tariffs, water charge reform; PostBank; cap unfair bank fees and credit card rates; rail fare cuts and stronger passenger rights.

Environment, housing, transport
- Zero‑carbon Britain by 2050; 40% clean electricity by 2020; offshore/marine focus; European Supergrid; block unabated coal; reject new nuclear; decade‑long home insulation offer up to £10k per home; public sector efficiency targets.
- More affordable, efficient homes; repossession as last resort; enable council housebuilding; scrap HIPs.
- Invest in rail (reopen lines, capacity), cut regulated fares RPI–1%; empower councils on buses; safer cycling; per‑plane duty; cancel Heathrow runway 3; roadmap to revenue‑neutral road pricing; rural fuel discount.
- Zero‑waste strategy; stronger biodiversity targets; expand access to countryside; double woodland by 2050; robust water/flood management.

Communities, crime, immigration, rural
- 3,000 more police, cut bureaucracy, elected police authorities; evidence‑based drugs policy focusing on treatment; restorative justice and neighbourhood panels.
- Firm but fair immigration: reintroduce exit checks; National Border Force; regional points‑based system; crack down on rogue employers; earned citizenship for long‑residing, law‑abiding migrants (pre‑2010). Asylum decisions by independent agency; end child detention; allow asylum seekers to work.
- Rural support: protect post offices (PostBank), fairer second‑home rules, farming regulator and CAP reform, support hill farmers.

Foreign policy and defence
- Lead EU/global action on climate, finance, and human rights; aid at 0.7% of GNI by 2013 in law; tougher stance on corruption/tax havens; support debt relief.
- SSDR; no like‑for‑like Trident; better pay and housing for lower ranks; European defence cooperation; principled stances on Afghanistan, Iran, arms trade, torture inquiry, and a two‑state solution for Israel–Palestine.

Political reform and civil liberties
- Fair votes (STV), reduce MPs by ~150; fixed‑term parliaments; elected second chamber; stronger Commons; written constitution via citizens’ convention.
- Right to recall MPs; cap donations at £10k; lobbyist register; UK‑tax‑resident legislators.
- Freedom Bill: regulate CCTV; protect protest/free speech; libel reform; scrap ID cards, ContactPoint and mass data retention; delete innocent DNA; keep Human Rights Act. Decentralise power and finance to local government; stronger Scottish/Welsh/Northern Irish settlements with needs‑based funding.
